claims.text: Two repository variants identify LeetCode 115 DP; the expanded variant additionally requires complexity analysis and a space-optimized solution.
Descending one-dimensional counting DP implements choose/not-choose without reusing a source index, in O(|s|*|t|) time and O(|t|) extra space.
Fixture validates official examples, positional combinations, boundaries, saturation and exhaustive bounded binary cases against an independent oracle.

findings: Both repository source variants resolve to LeetCode 115; the expanded source explicitly requires the s/t counting contract, time complexity analysis and a space optimization, all directly covered by the candidate.
The choose/not-choose recurrence is correct and the one-dimensional target index runs right-to-left, preserving the previous-source-prefix dependency so one source position is not reused in one scan.
The answer gives O(|s|*|t|) time and O(|t|) extra space and contrasts the direct two-dimensional O(|s|*|t|) storage.

The executable fixture verifies both official examples, positional duplicate counting, generalized DP bases, huge irrelevant intermediate-prefix saturation, and exhaustive bounded binary inputs against an independent recursive oracle.

Saturating nonnegative intermediate counts at Integer.MAX_VALUE+1 preserves every final answer within the official 32-bit promise: any saturated state that later contributes would force the downstream count above that promise; a saturated state that never contributes needs no exact larger magnitude.
No source variant is left uncovered and no project experience is fabricated. Formal promotion remains governed by repository promotion and real-review policy.
